purpose: Check whether the existing stateless ngram-simple mode has useful matches before running a hybrid MTP speed screen
input: Four measured baseline completions from pdl-off-20261021, with exact original prompts tokenized by the installed vocabulary-only tool
parameter_reason: Keep the default 12-token lookup. The current implementation rejects copy lengths smaller than the lookup length, so a maximum draft length of three would silently produce no drafts. Twelve is the smallest useful maximum without changing that implementation.
replay: Translate the pinned common_ngram_simple_draft search exactly. At every output position with 12 known future tokens, search only the prompt and earlier generated tokens; compare its proposal with the recorded future.
opportunity_gate: Consider a hybrid speed screen on these standard cases only if each case has at least one fully correct 12-token proposal. Do not sweep lookup lengths or draft lengths if either case fails.
limitations: This checks all possible output positions, not the actual MTP drafting boundaries
Recorded completions are development samples; repeated identical outputs are not independent evidence
Teacher-forced replay does not measure runtime latency, hybrid acceptance, numerical equivalence or quality
It cannot rule out benefits on separate copy-heavy or code-edit workloads
